lens: Boutique recruiter operational fit: GET-5-product-v1, baseline d363ac04 plus the manifest-frozen implementation. Synthetic independent recruiter juggling several searches on an iPhone, continuing a note through review, deliberate contact saving, restart and a fork. The intended success is one recoverable contact result and usable continuing context with the original source still inspectable. Actual search load, deadline pressure and field behavior are unavailable.

findings.criterion: Write safety: tell the recruiter whether the prior save is known to have failed
findings.observation: Direct observation: the response-loss screen simultaneously says that the previous outcome is unknown and that the contact was not saved. The frozen fallback error also makes the definite failure claim after an arbitrary save error. The native recovery subsequently finds the committed person and obtains the original-operation receipt. This is contradictory outcome communication, not evidence that the retry creates duplicate contacts.
findings.evidence: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/07-contact-response-lost-r6.png, pending-write banner and red contact-save error; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/08-contact-same-operation-restored-r6.png, Contact created receipt; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAskView.swift:5049-5053 and :5670-5694; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/UITests/CandidateSignalUITests.swift:5031-5068; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:552 records this response-loss/relaunch scenario passing.
findings.user_impact: Supported operational inference: a recruiter interrupted by a call can interpret the definite failure as permission to recreate the person manually, or distrust the later existing-person match. This adds reconciliation work despite the underlying protected retry.
findings.recommendation: Must fix before exposure: for an uncertain transport/readback outcome, use one consistent message such as “We could not confirm the save. Check the original save to recover its result.” Reserve “not saved” for a definitive rejection or a failure before submission. Keep the original operation locked and remove first-save-only assurances while its result is unknown.
findings.verification: Repeat the existing after-commit response-loss/relaunch scenario. Before reconciliation every visible outcome label must remain uncertain, and the existing same-operation identity/receipt assertions must still pass. Also inspect a definitive pre-submission failure to ensure it can truthfully say nothing was saved.

findings.criterion: Interruption recovery: distinguish the fork from the conversation the recruiter already used
findings.observation: Direct observation: after a successful fork and native back gesture, the Sessions list shows two rows with the identical title and the identical “Agent conversation” context. Relative time and a generic “Refresh needed” status are the only visible differences. The model already stores originSessionID, but the row does not communicate that origin.
findings.evidence: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/12-native-back-original-and-fork-r7.png, both visible Session rows; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveModels.swift:2655-2663 copies original.title and stores originSessionID; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:3579-3604 and :3644-3672 render title/context/accessibility label; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r7.log:676 records the fork/native-back scenario passing.
findings.user_impact: Supported operational inference: after switching between several searches or returning later, the recruiter must open conversations or remember their timestamps to find the intended branch. “Refresh needed” describes source state and is not a stable branch identifier.
findings.recommendation: Add a quiet, persistent fork label derived from the existing origin relationship to the Session row and its accessibility label, for example “Fork of …”. Preserve the original title and content. This is a small retrieval improvement; a branch-management feature is unnecessary.
findings.verification: Fork a Session, add a different follow-up in each branch, restart and return to the list. The original and fork must be distinguishable without opening either row, including when both answers need refresh. Confirm both still open their respective message histories.

strengths: Frozen provenance: independently recomputed SHA-256 for all 82 manifest entries; every hash matched. Observations use only GET-5-product-v1 frozen source, screenshots and logs. No implementation, service, Xcode or Simulator mutation was performed for this review.

Capture burden = 3/4. A natural name/email note prepares a draft without a separate entry form, and voice produces editable words without sending. Direct recorded proof: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/conversation-provider-proof.json:153-246; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/02-voice-draft.png; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:1012, :1060 and :1330. The voice test is deterministic Simulator input, not a speech-recognition accuracy result.

Evidence review = 3/4. Source message and exact field excerpts are inspectable beside the draft, with an explicit edit path and save gate. Source: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAskView.swift:5552-5567, :5762-5778 and :5881-5980. Missing relationship/save-disabled/decline behavior passed at /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:1287 with assertions in /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/UITests/Get5SessionUITests.swift:129-147. Correction effectiveness with real users is unproven.

State integrity = 3/4. The original source survives confirmation and restart, proposal expiry does not renew authority, and changing draft fields reruns lookup instead of silently reusing a selection. /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:704; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/09-original-message-and-receipt-r6.png; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-unit-r8.log:48-55 and :68-83; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAskView.swift:4828-4866 and :5119-5135. These are bounded executable checks, not full longitudinal field proof.

Action usefulness = 3/4 for the bounded contact-saving job. The recruiter deliberately saves one reviewed person/context, receives “Contact created”, can open People, and resumes the same conversation. /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/UITests/Get5CanonicalSessionUITests.swift:19-61; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:704; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/09-original-message-and-receipt-r6.png. This earns no claim that a candidate follow-up happened or momentum improved.

Write safety = 2/4, the material minimum. The same-operation recovery is executed and visible, but the contradictory failure copy in finding 1 weakens the user-visible result. /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:552; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/07-contact-response-lost-r6.png and screenshots/08-contact-same-operation-restored-r6.png.

Interruption recovery = 2/4. Contact restart and native back/fork preserve work, and interrupted screenshot input stays a typed recovery gate. Fork retrieval still requires unnecessary reconstruction. /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:704 and :1121; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r7.log:676; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/06-screenshot-recovery-r6.png and screenshots/12-native-back-original-and-fork-r7.png. Cross-device/day return with changed outside state has not been observed here.

Wedge discipline = 3/4. The inspected Session surfaces focus on capture, source inspection, deliberate contact review and readable continuation. Screenshot processing details are secondary and the inline result states that no action was taken. Forks remove pending authority. /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/10-screenshot-inline-r6.png; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveModels.swift:2646-2663; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-unit-r8.log:56-57. No person scoring is visible in these inspected surfaces.
missing_evidence: Trigger relevance = 2/4. The scenario has a plausible recent-conversation trigger, but the frozen brief does not specify active-search count, an actual candidate/client decision deadline or competing work. The screenshot fixture uses an unresolved Friday without date/timezone (/tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAskView.swift:3577-3589). Add one realistic interrupted search task before treating this as a complete workflow test.

Must test with recruiters / value hypothesis: no observed comparison against copying a note or adding the contact manually establishes lower total effort, fewer missed commitments, or reduced correction burden. Use a small moderated task with seeded wrong-person/purpose errors and an interruption; measure source checking, corrections, duplicate entry, time to verified result and return-to-task accuracy. Do not turn this hypothesis into a field-usefulness claim.

The canonical provider trial proves that prior dialogue is supplied and “option two” is continued. Its generic request produces an applicant-to-recruiter email (/tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/conversation-provider-proof.json:280-300), so it does not establish usefulness for a recruiter-owned candidate follow-up. That request is ambiguous; this review does not classify the result as a confirmed routing defect. Test an explicit recruiter-to-candidate task with a concrete role, commitment and unresolved constraint.

The frozen screenshot UI case did not complete in either r6 or r7 (/tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:759-761 and get5-ios-ui-final-r7.log:389-391). The inspected inline image establishes rendering, not the full source-inspection/follow-up chain. The documented fixture startup/selector problem does not establish production upload failure. Root owns the remaining native screenshot and final actual-provider verification.

Same-account concurrent-message behavior is exercised in store tests (/tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-unit-r8.log:76-83), but there is no observed two-device/next-day task with a changed contact or withdrawn source. The backend 121-test result is stated in BRIEF.md without its own executable log in this manifest; this review does not upgrade that statement to directly inspected runtime proof.

Screenshot recovery requires the same images in the same order and keeps the composer disabled (/tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/06-screenshot-recovery-r6.png; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/UITests/Get5SessionUITests.swift:151-172). The fallback when those images can no longer be reselected is untested. Establish how the recruiter resumes useful work while retaining an honest unresolved operation; the evidence does not justify removing the protected recovery gate.

Provider evidence is a bounded earlier recorded trial: several provider-proof source_sha256 values differ from the final manifest (/tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/conversation-provider-proof.json:20-23). Final screenshot GLM trials, local TestFlight rebuild, deployed-source parity and physical-device VoiceOver are outside this packet and are not claimed complete.
